mainTopic: The best way to give צדקה, the power of צדקה, and whether the nations' charity counts as merit
overview: This amud finishes the גמרא's answer about the best kind of צדקה. It is best when the giver and the receiver don't know each other, which rules out the methods of מר עוקבא and רבי אבא. The practical way to do this is to give through the community charity fund, as long as someone as honest as רבי חנניא בן תרדיון runs it. Next come teachings in praise of צדקה from רבי אבהו and רבי אבא, and a story where יוסף בן רבי יהושע glimpses the next world and sees that Torah scholars and martyrs hold high places there. Then a ברייתא brings רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's students explaining the פסוק 'צדקה תרומם גוי וחסד לאמים חטאת'. Most of them read it as saying the nations' kindness counts as sin because of their motives. רבי נחוניא בן הקנה gives a different reading, and רבן יוחנן בן זכאי himself says צדקה atones for the nations the way a חטאת offering atones for ישראל. The amud ends with the story of the queen mother's gift to רבי אמי and רבא, and the explanation of רבי אמי's anger continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ideal kind of charity: giver and receiver don't know each other
steps.stepSummary: The best צדקה is given so that the giver doesn't know who receives it, and the receiver doesn't know who gave it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He gives it without knowing to whom he gives it, and the other takes it without knowing from whom he takes it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its answer to an earlier question about what kind of צדקה saves a person from death. The answer: complete two-way secrecy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate conditions are given here. The giver must not know the receiver, and the receiver must not know the giver. Having only one of them is not the top level.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the standard for the highest level of giving, which protects the poor person from embarrassment.

phrases.english: He gives it, and does not know to whom he gives it,
phrases.notes: This finishes an answer that began before this section: which צדקה saves a person from an unnatural death.

phrases.english: he (the poor person) takes it, and does not know from whom he takes it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the answer to the question asked just before this section.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The best צדקה involves secrecy in both directions: giver and receiver do not know each other.

steps.title: Each condition rules out a famous practice
steps.stepSummary: The first condition rules out the way מר עוקבא gave, and the second rules out the way רבי אבא gave.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He gives without knowing to whom' comes to exclude the way of מר עוקבא. 'He takes without knowing from whom' comes to exclude the way of רבי אבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why each half of the rule is needed. Each half rules out a real method that a great sage used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר עוקבא gave secretly, so the poor didn't know it was him, but he knew who got the money. רבי אבא left money for the poor to take, so he didn't know who took it, but they knew it came from him. Each method had only half of the secrecy, so neither is the top level.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא famous for giving צדקה secretly
An אמורא famous for leaving money out for the poor to take

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not criticizing these sages as doing something wrong. It is only saying their way is not the very highest level of this specific kind of צדקה.

phrases.english: 'He gives it and does not know to whom he gives it' –
comes to exclude the way of מר עוקבא;
phrases.notes: מר עוקבא secretly gave to poor people he knew, so they didn't know the giver, but he knew who got it.

phrases.english: 'He takes it and does not know from whom he takes it' –
comes to exclude the way of רבי אבא.
phrases.notes: רבי אבא left money out for the poor to take, so he didn't know who took it, but they knew it was his.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why each of the two conditions in step 1 is needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each half of the rule rules out a known method with only one-sided secrecy (מר עוקבא, רבי אבא).

steps.title: So how should a person give?
steps.stepSummary: If both great sages' methods fall short, what is the right way to give?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, how should one act?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question that sets up the next step. If those two methods aren't ideal, what method is?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two-way secrecy seems hard to achieve when you give in person. The question asks for a practical method that meets both conditions.

phrases.english: Rather, how should one act?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 2: both known methods were ruled out.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical method of giving with secrecy on both sides.

steps.title: Put the money in the community charity fund
steps.stepSummary: The answer: give into the public charity fund, where neither side knows the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: He should put it into the charity fund.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: give through the community's charity fund. The fund passes the money along, so giver and receiver stay unknown to each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A middleman fund solves both problems at once. The giver doesn't pick the poor person, and the poor person gets the money from the fund, not from a known giver.

keyTerms.meaning: The charity purse, the community fund for צדקה

steps.whatToRemember: The top level of this kind of צדקה is two-way secrecy, and the practical way to get it is giving through the community charity fund.

phrases.english: He should give it into the charity fund.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Give into the ארנקי של צדקה (community charity fund).

steps.title: A ברייתא warns against giving to the charity fund
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: don't give even a פרוטה to the charity fund unless someone like רבי חנניא בן תרדיון runs it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: What should a person do to have sons? רבי אליעזר says: he should spread his money among the poor. רבי יהושע says: he should make his wife happy for the מצוה. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: a person should not give a פרוטה to the charity fund unless someone like רבי חנניא בן תרדיון is in charge of it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 4 with a ברייתא. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב seems to say the charity fund is not always a good place to give.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said the charity fund is the ideal way to give. But רבי אליעזר בן יעקב warns against giving there unless the person in charge is completely trustworthy. So it seems the fund is not automatically the best choice.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a ברייתא)
He should spread out, distribute generously
A תנא known for his great honesty in managing צדקה funds

steps.confusionAlert: The first two opinions (about having sons) are not the challenge. They are simply part of the same ברייתא. Only רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's line is the problem for step 4.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: What should a person do
so that he will have male children?

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: יְפַזֵּר מְעוֹתָיו לַעֲנִיִּים.
phrases.english: רבי אליעזר says: He should distribute his money to the poor.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: יְשַׂמַּח אִשְׁתּוֹ לִדְבַר מִצְוָה.
phrases.english: רבי יהושע says: He should make his wife happy for the מצוה.
phrases.notes: The 'מצוה' here means marital relations.

phrases.english: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִתֵּן אָדָם פְּרוּטָה לְאַרְנָקִי שֶׁל צְדָקָה,
phrases.english: A person should not give a פרוטה to the charity fund,
unless there is appointed over it
someone like רבי חנניא בן תרדיון!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: מָה יַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם וְיִהְיוּ לוֹ בָּנִים זְכָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 4's claim that the ideal way to give is through the charity fund.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says not to give to the fund unless it has a fully trustworthy manager, so the fund cannot simply be called the ideal.

steps.title: We meant a fund run by someone trustworthy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: when we said to give to the fund, we meant a fund managed by someone like רבי חנניא בן תרדיון.
steps.simpleTranslation: When we said it, it was where someone like רבי חנניא בן תרדיון is in charge of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing its own statement. The charity fund is ideal only when an honest person runs it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is really no argument. Both sources agree that a fund is ideal when the manager is trustworthy. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב was only warning about funds without such a manager.

keyTerms.meaning: When we said (it was in this case)
That he is appointed over it

steps.whatToRemember: Giving through the charity fund is the ideal, but only if a fully trustworthy person manages it.

phrases.english: When we said it (that one should give to the fund) –

phrases.aramaic: דִּמְמַנֵּי עֲלַהּ כְּרַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא בֶּן תְּרַדְיוֹן.
phrases.english: it was where someone like רבי חנניא בן תרדיון is appointed over it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the earlier statement applies only to a trustworthy fund.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Step 4 seemed to say any charity fund is ideal, which would conflict with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Step 4 meant only a fund run by someone like רבי חנניא בן תרדיון, so both sources agree.

steps.title: משה asks how Israel will be raised up
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says: משה asked הקב"ה how Israel's 'horn' would be raised, and הקב"ה answered: through 'כי תשא', meaning through giving.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: משה said before הקב"ה: Master of the world, through what will the horn of Israel be raised? He said to him: through 'כי תשא'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to teachings in praise of צדקה. רבי אבהו says Israel is raised up through giving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'כי תשא' mean 'when you raise', and they open the section where each Jew gives a half-shekel. The play on words teaches that giving is what raises Israel's standing.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'horn' of Israel, its strength and honor
'When you raise': the opening of the half-shekel section

phrases.english: רבי אבהו said,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מֹשֶׁה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: משה said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the world,
through what will the horn of Israel be raised?
He said to him: through 'When you raise'.
phrases.notes: שמות 30:12, the section where each person gives a half-shekel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ, אָמַר מֹשֶׁה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section of אגדה in praise of צדקה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Israel is raised up through giving, hinted in 'כי תשא'.

steps.title: How far does the power of charity reach?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says: people asked King שלמה how great the power of צדקה is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אבהו said: They asked שלמה son of דוד: How far does the power of צדקה reach?
steps.whatsHappening: A second teaching of רבי אבהו begins with a question to King שלמה. It sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about the limit of צדקה's power, meaning how much good it can bring the giver.

phrases.english: And רבי אבהו said,
They asked שלמה son of דוד:
How far does the power of צדקה reach?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ, שָׁאֲלוּ אֶת שְׁלֹמֹה בֶּן דָּוִד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching of רבי אבהו on the same theme.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How great the power of צדקה is.

steps.title: שלמה answers with his father's פסוק
steps.stepSummary: שלמה points to a פסוק by דוד: one who gives to the poor, his righteousness lasts forever and his horn is raised with honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Go and see what my father דוד explained: 'He distributed, he gave to the poor; his righteousness stands forever; his horn will be raised with honor.'
steps.whatsHappening: שלמה answers by quoting a פסוק from תהלים. Its message is that giving to the poor brings lasting merit and honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer to 'how far' is 'forever': the merit of צדקה never ends. The words 'his horn will be raised' tie back to משה's question in step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: He distributed, he gave to the poor

phrases.english: He said to them,

phrases.aramaic: צְאוּ וּרְאוּ מָה פֵּירֵשׁ דָּוִד אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Go out and see what my father דוד explained:
'He distributed, he gave to the poor –
his righteousness stands forever,
his horn will be raised with honor.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 112:9

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן, צְאוּ וּרְאוּ מָה פֵּירֵשׁ דָּוִד אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The merit of צדקה lasts forever and raises the giver with honor (תהלים 112:9).

steps.title: רבי אבא brings a different פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא learns the power of צדקה from a פסוק in ישעיהו about dwelling on high.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: from here: 'He will dwell on high, fortresses of rock are his stronghold, his bread is given, his water is faithful.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא gives another source for how great צדקה is. He quotes a פסוק from ישעיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a different פסוק for the same idea. The פסוק links being raised up and protected to giving bread and water.

phrases.english: רבי אבא said: it is learned from here:
'He will dwell on high,
fortresses of rock are his stronghold,
his bread is given, his water is faithful';
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 33:16

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different פסוק for the same idea as step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The power of צדקה is learned from ישעיהו 33:16.

steps.title: Why he dwells on high: because he gives
steps.stepSummary: The reason the person dwells on high and is protected is that he gives his bread and water to the poor faithfully.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does 'he dwell on high, fortresses of rock are his stronghold'? Because 'his bread is given' and 'his water is faithful'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא explains how to read the פסוק. The second half (giving) is the reason for the first half (being raised up and protected).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read plainly, the פסוק looks like a list of blessings. רבי אבא reads it as cause and effect: because the person gives faithfully, he is raised up and safe.

keyTerms.meaning: His bread is given (to the poor)

steps.whatToRemember: צדקה raises the giver up: Israel is raised through giving (רבי אבהו), its merit lasts forever (שלמה), and it brings a person height and protection (רבי אבא).

phrases.english: What is the reason that 'he will dwell on high,
fortresses of rock are his stronghold' –
because 'his bread is given'
and 'his water is faithful'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק in step 10 proves the power of צדקה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Being raised up and protected comes because of faithful giving of bread and water.

steps.title: Who is destined for עולם הבא?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו reports another question people asked שלמה: who is a בן עולם הבא?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אבהו said: They asked שלמה: Who is someone destined for עולם הבא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another question that people asked שלמה. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the series of רבי אבהו's reports about questions put to שלמה. Now the topic shifts from the power of צדקה to the question of who earns a place in עולם הבא.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Abbahu said:
They asked Solomon:
Who is one destined for the World-to-Come?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ, שָׁאֲלוּ אֶת שְׁלֹמֹה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another report by רבי אבהו of a question asked of שלמה, now on a new topic.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of person is destined for עולם הבא?

steps.title: Those honored before the elders
steps.stepSummary: שלמה answers with a פסוק: anyone of whom it is said 'before His elders is glory'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Anyone of whom it says, 'And before His elders shall be glory.'
steps.whatsHappening: שלמה answers by quoting a פסוק from ישעיהו about glory given before the elders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer ties a place in עולם הבא to the honor of the 'elders'. The next story shows what this honor looks like in the next world.

phrases.english: He said to them:
Anyone of whom it says: "before His elders is glory."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 24:23.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Those described by the פסוק 'before His elders is glory' are destined for עולם הבא.

steps.title: יוסף sees an upside-down world
steps.stepSummary: יוסף בריה דרבי יהושע faints and sees a world where the important are low and the lowly are high. His father calls it a 'clear world'.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like the case of יוסף, the son of רבי יהושע, who became ill and fainted. His father asked him: What did you see? He said: I saw an upside-down world. Those above were below, and those below were above. His father said: You saw a clear world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story to show what the honor of the next world looks like. יוסף saw that people's rank there is very different from their rank here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Those who are important in this world are low in the next, and the reverse. רבי יהושע says this is not 'upside-down' at all. It is the true, clear picture of how people really stand.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּיוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Like this case of Yosef, son of Rabbi Yehoshua:
he became ill and fainted.
His father said to him: What did you see?
He said to him: I saw an upside-down world:
those above were below,
and those below were above.
He said to him: You saw a clear world.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּיוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the answer of step 13 with a story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The next world shows people's true rank, which is often the reverse of their rank in this world.

steps.title: How are Torah scholars seen there?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע asks his son how the Torah scholars appear in that world.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how did you see us?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע asks a follow-up question: where do people like us, the Torah scholars, stand in that world? This sets up his son's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If rank flips over in the next world, one might worry that Torah scholars are also brought down. The question checks whether they are an exception.

phrases.english: And us, how did you see us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follow-up question within the story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the standing of Torah scholars in the next world?

steps.title: Scholars are important there too
steps.stepSummary: יוסף answers: just as Torah scholars are important here, they are important there.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Just as we are important here, we are important there.
steps.whatsHappening: יוסף answers that Torah scholars keep their high standing in the next world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Torah scholars are the exception to the 'upside-down' rule. Their honor here is real, so it stays the same there. This fits the פסוק about glory before the elders.
steps.whatToRemember: In the next world, worldly rank may flip, but the honor of Torah scholars stays the same.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Just as we are important here,
we are important there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Torah scholars are just as important in the next world as in this one.

steps.title: Happy is one who arrives with his learning
steps.stepSummary: יוסף reports hearing that one who arrives in the next world with his learning in hand is fortunate.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I heard them saying: Happy is the one who comes here with his learning in his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: יוסף adds something else he heard in the next world: praise for one who arrives with his Torah learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds to the theme that Torah gives lasting standing. 'In his hand' suggests learning that he still has and remembers, not just something he once studied.

phrases.english: And I heard that they were saying:
Happy is the one who comes here
with his learning in his hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Further report from יוסף's vision.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who reaches the next world with his Torah learning is fortunate.

steps.title: No one can stand in the section of the martyrs
steps.stepSummary: יוסף heard that no one can stand in the section of הרוגי מלכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I heard them saying: Those killed by the government, no creature can stand in their section.
steps.whatsHappening: יוסף reports one more thing he heard: those killed by the government have a place so high that no one else can reach it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This gives martyrs a unique, very high level in the next world. It is not yet clear which martyrs are meant, and the גמרא asks about that next.

phrases.english: And I heard that they were saying:
Those killed by the government:
no creature is able
to stand in their section.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another report from the same vision.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Martyrs killed by the government hold an unreachable level in the next world.

steps.title: Who are these martyrs?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which martyrs יוסף meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who are they?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which martyrs this statement is talking about. This sets up a suggestion and its rejection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The statement only says 'those killed by the government' without names. The גמרא wants to know who is meant so the praise makes sense.

phrases.english: Who are they?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the identity of the martyrs mentioned in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which martyrs are the הרוגי מלכות in יוסף's report?

steps.title: Not רבי עקיבא and his colleagues
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests רבי עקיבא and his colleagues but rejects it: their greatness is obvious even without their martyrdom.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means רבי עקיבא and his colleagues, is it only because they were killed by the government and nothing more? It is obvious that even without this they are great!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible answer and throws it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא and his colleagues were already giants in their lives. Saying their level comes from being martyred would add nothing new, because their greatness is obvious anyway. So the statement must mean someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion about to be rejected)

phrases.english: If you say it means Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues,
is it because they were killed by the government, and nothing more?!
It is obvious that even without this, they would be great too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes and rejects an answer to step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the martyrs are רבי עקיבא and his colleagues.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Their high level is obvious without their martyrdom, so the statement would teach nothing.

steps.title: It means הרוגי לוד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the statement refers to הרוגי לוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means the martyrs of לוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer: the martyrs meant are הרוגי לוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After rejecting רבי עקיבא, the גמרא picks martyrs whose high level comes from the martyrdom itself. That makes the statement teach something new.
steps.whatToRemember: The unreachable level of martyrs refers to הרוגי לוד, whose great standing comes from their martyrdom itself.

phrases.english: Rather, it means the martyrs of Lod.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the accepted answer after the rejection in step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The martyrs referred to are הרוגי לוד.

steps.title: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי asks about a verse
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי asks his students the meaning of 'צדקה תרומם גוי וחסד לאמים חטאת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי said to his students: My sons, what does the פסוק mean: 'Righteousness exalts a nation, and the kindness of the peoples is sin'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבן יוחנן בן זכאי asks his students to explain a פסוק in משלי. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic goes back to צדקה. The פסוק seems strange: how can kindness be called 'sin'? This puzzle drives the explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: The kindness of the peoples is sin

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי לְתַלְמִידָיו:
phrases.english: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai said to his students:
My sons, what is the meaning of what the verse says:
"Righteousness exalts a nation,
phrases.notes: משלי 14:34.

phrases.english: and the kindness of the peoples is sin"?

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר לָהֶן רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי לְתַלְמִידָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section about צדקה, using a ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the meaning of the פסוק 'צדקה תרומם גוי וחסד לאמים חטאת'?

steps.title: The 'nation' raised by righteousness is Israel
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר explains that the first half of the פסוק refers to ישראל, proven by a פסוק calling ישראל 'one nation'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר answered: 'Righteousness exalts a nation' means ישראל, as it is written: 'And who is like Your people ישראל, one nation on the earth.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר begins his answer by explaining who the 'nation' in the first half of the פסוק is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He shows from a פסוק in דברי הימים that ישראל is called 'גוי'. So the צדקה that raises up a 'nation' is the צדקה of ישראל.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer answered and said:
"Righteousness exalts a nation": these are Israel,
as it is written:
"And who is like Your people Israel,
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 17:21.

phrases.english: one nation on the earth."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First half of the answer to step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'nation' raised by צדקה is ישראל.

steps.title: The nations' kindness counts as sin
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר explains that the nations' charity and kindness is a sin for them, because they do it only for self-glory, as seen in a פסוק in עזרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the kindness of the peoples is sin' means: all the charity and kindness the nations of the world do is a sin for them, because they do it only to make themselves great. As it says: 'So that they may offer pleasing offerings to the God of heaven, and pray for the life of the king and his sons.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר explains the second half of the פסוק: the nations' good deeds are counted as sin because of why they do them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not the act but the goal: they give only to raise their own glory. The proof from עזרא shows a king supporting offerings so that people would pray for him and his sons, meaning for his own benefit.

phrases.english: "And the kindness of the peoples is sin":
all the charity and kindness
that the nations of the world do
is a sin for them;
because they do not do it
except to make themselves great through it,
as it is said:
"That they may offer
phrases.notes: עזרא 6:10. This is Aramaic, said by the king who funded the offerings.

phrases.english: pleasing offerings to the God of heaven,
and pray for the life of the king and his sons."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of רבי אליעזר's answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The nations' kindness is counted as sin because it is done only for self-glory.

steps.title: But giving for personal benefit is called fully righteous
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: a ברייתא says one who gives a סלע to צדקה so his children will live, or to earn עולם הבא, is a צדיק גמור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one who acts this way, is it not complete צדקה? But it was taught: One who says, 'This סלע is for צדקה so that my sons will live,' or 'so that I will merit עולם הבא,' is a צדיק גמור!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי אליעזר's explanation using a ברייתא that praises giving even with a personal goal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר said giving for one's own benefit turns kindness into sin. But the ברייתא says giving to save one's children or to earn עולם הבא still makes a person a צדיק גמור. These two sources seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught (introduces a challenge)

phrases.english: And one who acts this way,
is it not complete charity?!
But it was taught in a baraita: One who says:
"This sela is for charity,
so that my sons will live,"
or "so that I will merit the World-to-Come":
this is a completely righteous person!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּדְעָבֵיד הָכִי, לָאו צְדָקָה גְּמוּרָה הִיא?! וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the idea in step 24 that giving for self-benefit is not real צדקה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's claim that kindness done for personal gain counts as sin.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא calls someone who gives for personal benefit a צדיק גמור, so personal motive does not cancel the צדקה.

steps.title: One source is about a Jew, the other about a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: the ברייתא about a צדיק גמור speaks of a Jew, while רבי אליעזר's statement speaks of a non-Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here it is talking about a Jew, and there it is talking about a non-Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying each source talks about a different kind of person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Jew who gives for a personal goal is still a צדיק גמור, as the ברייתא says. A non-Jew who gives only to glorify himself is the case רבי אליעזר meant. So the two sources do not argue.

keyTerms.meaning: Here... there (each source fits a different case)

steps.whatToRemember: A Jew who gives צדקה with a personal goal is still a צדיק גמור. רבי אליעזר's 'kindness is sin' applies to the nations, who give only for self-glory.
steps.confusionAlert: Keep track of which 'here' goes with which source: 'בישראל' matches the ברייתא of the צדיק גמור, and 'בגוי' matches רבי אליעזר's explanation.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here it is about a Jew,
there it is about a non-Jew.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא; כָּאן בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, כָּאן בְּגוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting cases: each source refers to a different person.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources speak about the same giver, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא praising giving for personal benefit refers to a Jew. The statement that such giving is sin refers to a non-Jew.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: The nations give charity to keep their kingdom
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע agrees the first half of the פסוק is about ישראל. He says the nations' charity is a sin because they give only so their rule will last, and he proves it from דניאל's advice to the king.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע answered: 'Righteousness exalts a nation' means Israel, as it says 'Who is like Your people Israel, one nation.' 'The kindness of the peoples is sin' means all the charity and kindness the nations do is a sin for them, because they do it only so their kingdom will last. As it says: 'Therefore, O king, accept my advice: break off your sins with charity and your wrongdoings by being kind to the poor, so that your peace may last longer.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second student, רבי יהושע, gives his explanation of the same פסוק. He agrees with רבי אליעזר about ישראל but gives a new reason why the nations' kindness counts as a sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר said the nations give for their own glory. רבי יהושע says they give to make their kingdom last longer. His proof is the פסוק in דניאל, where the reason offered to the king for giving charity is that it will extend his peace and rule, so the motive is selfish.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua answered and said:
"Righteousness exalts a nation": these are Israel,
as it is written: "And who is like Your people Israel, one nation";
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 17:21

phrases.english: "But the kindness of the peoples is sin":

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל צְדָקָה וָחֶסֶד שֶׁאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם עוֹשִׂין,
phrases.english: all the charity and kindness that the nations of the world do
is a sin for them;

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין אֶלָּא כְּדֵי שֶׁתִּמָּשֵׁךְ מַלְכוּתָן,
phrases.english: because they do it only so that their kingdom will last,
as it is said: "Therefore, O king, let my advice be pleasing to you,
phrases.notes: דניאל 4:24

phrases.english: and break off your sins with charity,
and your wrongdoings by being kind to the poor,
so that there may be a lengthening of your peace, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא after the גמרא's side question (Steps 25-26) and gives a second student's answer to רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The nations' charity is a sin because it is done only to make their kingdom last, as shown by דניאל's advice to the king.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל: The nations give charity to show off
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל says the nations give charity only to act proud, and a proud person falls into גיהנם, based on two פסוקים linked by the word עברה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל answered: 'Righteousness exalts a nation' means Israel, as it says 'Who is like Your people Israel.' 'The kindness of the peoples is sin' means all the charity and kindness the nations do is a sin for them, because they do it only to act proud, and anyone who acts proud falls into גיהנם. As it says: 'The proud, haughty man, scorner is his name, acts with arrogant wrath (עברה).' And 'wrath' means גיהנם, as it says: 'That day is a day of wrath.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third student, רבן גמליאל, explains the פסוק. He agrees about ישראל but says the nations' motive is arrogance, and arrogance leads to גיהנם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His proof has two links. First, a פסוק in משלי says the arrogant person acts with 'עברה'. Then a פסוק in צפניה uses 'עברה' for the day of punishment, which he reads as גיהנם, so the arrogant one ends up in גיהנם.

keyTerms.meaning: to act proud / to show off

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel answered and said:
"Righteousness exalts a nation": these are Israel,
as it is written: "And who is like Your people Israel, etc.";
"But the kindness of the peoples is sin":
all the charity and kindness that the gentiles do
is a sin for them;
because they do it only to act proud with it,
and anyone who acts proud falls into Gehinnom,
as it is said: "The proud, haughty man, scorner is his name,
phrases.notes: משלי 21:24

phrases.english: acts with arrogant wrath";
and "wrath" means nothing other than Gehinnom,
as it is said: "That day is a day of wrath."
phrases.notes: צפניה 1:15

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the same question, with a different motive: arrogance instead of keeping their kingdom.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The nations' charity is a sin because they do it to show off, and the arrogant fall into גיהנם.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר המודעי: The nations give charity to taunt Israel
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל says they still need to hear the view of the מודעי. רבי אליעזר המודעי says the nations do kindness only to taunt ישראל, as when a Babylonian commander told the Jews their troubles came because they sinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said: We still need the מודעי. רבי אליעזר המודעי says: 'Righteousness exalts a nation' means Israel, as it says 'Who is like Your people Israel, one nation.' 'The kindness of the peoples is sin' means all the charity and kindness the nations do is a sin for them, because they do it only to taunt us with it. As it says: 'ה׳ brought it and did as He said, because you sinned against ה׳ and did not listen to His voice, so this thing has happened to you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל points out that one more opinion is still needed, the view of רבי אליעזר המודעי. That view is then quoted: the nations' kindness is meant to mock ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a fourth motive: not glory, not keeping the kingdom, not arrogance, but taunting ישראל. The פסוק in ירמיהו shows a gentile who treats the Jews 'kindly' while telling them that their suffering is their own fault for sinning.

keyTerms.meaning: the man from מודיעין (רבי אליעזר המודעי)

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel said:
We still need the Moda'i,
phrases.notes: We still need to hear what רבי אליעזר המודעי says about this פסוק.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer HaModa'i says:
"Righteousness exalts a nation": these are Israel,
as it is written: "And who is like Your people Israel, one nation";
"But the kindness of the peoples is sin":

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל צְדָקָה וָחֶסֶד שֶׁאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם עוֹשִׂין,
phrases.english: all the charity and kindness that the nations of the world do
is a sin for them;

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין אֶלָּא לְחָרֵף אוֹתָנוּ בּוֹ,
phrases.english: because they do it only to taunt us with it,
as it is said: "ה׳ brought it and did as He said,
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 40:3, words spoken to the Jews by the Babylonian commander.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי חֲטָאתֶם לַה׳ וְלֹא שְׁמַעְתֶּם בְּקוֹלוֹ,
phrases.english: because you sinned against ה׳ and did not listen to His voice,
so this thing has happened to you."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: עֲדַיִין אָנוּ צְרִיכִין לַמּוֹדָעִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבן גמליאל, who just gave his own answer, brings in one more opinion, which gives a fourth motive.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The nations' kindness is a sin because they use it to taunt ישראל.

steps.title: רבי נחוניא בן הקנה divides the verse differently
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחוניא בן הקנה reads both 'righteousness' and 'kindness' as belonging to ישראל, and only 'sin' as belonging to the nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחוניא בן הקנה answered: 'Righteousness exalts a nation, and kindness': these are for Israel. And 'for the peoples: sin.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another student, רבי נחוניא בן הקנה, gives a new reading. Instead of saying the nations have kindness that turns into sin, he moves 'kindness' to the ישראל half of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answers read 'the kindness of the peoples' as one phrase, so they had to explain why the nations' kindness is bad. רבי נחוניא splits the פסוק after 'וחסד', so ישראל have righteousness and kindness, and the nations have only sin. This avoids calling real kindness a sin.

keyTerms.meaning: sin (also the name of the sin-offering)

phrases.aramaic: נַעֲנָה רַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא בֶּן הַקָּנָה וְאָמַר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKana answered and said:
"Righteousness exalts a nation, and kindness": for Israel;
and "for the peoples: sin."

steps.triggerLanguage: נַעֲנָה רַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא בֶּן הַקָּנָה וְאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Breaks from the shared pattern of the earlier answers by dividing the פסוק in a different place.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Righteousness and kindness both belong to ישראל; the nations get only sin.

steps.title: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי prefers רבי נחוניא's reading
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי tells his students that רבי נחוניא בן הקנה's explanation is better than his own and theirs, because it gives righteousness and kindness to ישראל and sin to the nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי said to his students: The words of רבי נחוניא בן הקנה seem better than my words and your words, because he gives righteousness and kindness to Israel, and sin to the nations.
steps.whatsHappening: The teacher who asked the question now judges the answers. He picks רבי נחוניא בן הקנה's reading as the best.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reason is that רבי נחוניא keeps all the good, righteousness and kindness, for ישראל and leaves only sin for the nations. Notice that he says 'my words', which hints that he also gave an explanation. The גמרא picks up on that next.

keyTerms.meaning: than my words and than your words

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי לְתַלְמִידָיו:
phrases.english: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai said to his students:

phrases.aramaic: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא בֶּן הַקָּנָה
phrases.english: The words of Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKana seem better
than my words and than your words,

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁהוּא נוֹתֵן צְדָקָה וָחֶסֶד לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: because he gives righteousness and kindness to Israel,
and sin to the nations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי לְתַלְמִידָיו: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Judges between the students' answers and chooses רבי נחוניא's.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי נחוניא בן הקנה's reading is preferred: righteousness and kindness go to ישראל, sin goes to the nations.

steps.title: The גמרא asks what רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's own explanation was
steps.stepSummary: From the words 'than my words', the גמרא infers that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי also had an explanation, and asks what it was.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that he also said an explanation. What is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps out of the ברייתא to ask a question. This sets up the next step, where his explanation will be quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי compared רבי נחוניא's words to 'my words', yet no explanation of his appears in this ברייתא. So the גמרא asks where his own reading is found.

phrases.english: This implies that he also said an explanation;
What is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּהוּא נָמֵי אָמַר; מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Infers from רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's phrase 'my words' that he had his own reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What was רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's own explanation of the פסוק?

steps.title: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי: Charity atones for the nations like a sin-offering
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבן יוחנן בן זכאי: just as the חטאת offering atones for ישראל, so charity atones for the nations of the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי said to them: Just as the חטאת offering atones for Israel, so צדקה atones for the nations of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting a ברייתא with רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's own reading. He reads 'חטאת' in the פסוק as the sin-offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For him the פסוק is positive about the nations. 'Righteousness' (צדקה) works for the nations ('לאמים') the way a חטאת offering works for ישראל: it brings them atonement.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is taught (in a ברייתא)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'חטאת' here as 'sin' as the other answers did. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי means the קרבן called חטאת, the sin-offering, which brings atonement.
steps.whatToRemember: Every student read 'חטאת' as 'sin' and gave a reason the nations' kindness is faulty: glory, keeping their kingdom, showing off, or taunting. רבי נחוניא moved 'kindness' to ישראל and was praised. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי himself read 'חטאת' as the sin-offering: charity atones for the nations as the קרבן atones for ישראל.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר לָהֶם רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי:
phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai said to them:
Just as the sin-offering atones for Israel,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ צְדָקָה מְכַפֶּרֶת עַל אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם.
phrases.english: so charity atones for the nations of the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר לָהֶם רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 32 by quoting a ברייתא with רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's own explanation.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי read the פסוק as: charity atones for the nations just as a חטאת offering atones for ישראל.
steps.whyThisMatters: Unlike his students' readings, this one treats the nations' charity as truly valuable. It brings them atonement.

steps.title: The queen mother sends charity money
steps.stepSummary: איפרא הורמיז sends 400 dinars to רבי אמי, who refuses them. She then sends them to רבא, who accepts them for the sake of שלום מלכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: איפרא הורמיז, mother of King שבור, sent 400 dinars to רבי אמי, and he would not take them. She sent them to רבא, and he took them to keep peace with the kingdom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a non-Jewish queen mother who gave charity money to two different חכמים. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story connects to the earlier statements that the nations' kindness is not counted as true merit. Two great אמוראים react in opposite ways to the same gift. One refuses it, and the other accepts it because of a practical concern, שלום מלכות.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace with the government; keeping good relations with the ruling power

phrases.english: Ifra Hurmiz, the mother of King Shapur,
sent four hundred dinars
to Rabbi Ami, and he did not accept them.
She sent them to Rava,
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets are the corrected spelling, which makes it clear that she was the one who sent them.

phrases.english: and he accepted them for the sake of peace with the kingdom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real-life story about charity from the nations, following the earlier discussion of whether such charity counts as merit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אמי refused the queen mother's charity, while רבא accepted it for the sake of שלום מלכות.

steps.title: רבי אמי objects to רבא using a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי hears what רבא did, gets angry, and cites a פסוק from ישעיהו to show that one should not take charity from the nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי heard and got angry. He said: Does רבא not hold of the פסוק, "When its branches dry up they will be broken, women will come and burn it"?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי challenges רבא's choice by quoting a פסוק. He holds that accepting the money was wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי reads the פסוק to mean that once a nation's merit has dried up, it is time for it to be punished. Taking their charity gives them new merit and delays that punishment, so a Jew should not help them do it.

keyTerms.meaning: Does he not hold of? (literally, he does not have)

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami heard, became angry, and said:
Does he not hold of the verse:
"When its boughs are withered, they shall be broken off;
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 27:11. He means: once a nation's merit dries up, it should be 'broken', so don't give it new merit.

phrases.english: women shall come and set it on fire"?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי אמי reacts critically to רבא's acceptance of the money.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's decision to accept the queen mother's charity
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק shows that the nations should not be given chances to gain merit, and accepting their charity gives them that merit.

steps.title: רבא acted for the sake of peace with the kingdom
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא accepted the money and answers that he did it for שלום מלכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא? He did it for the sake of peace with the kingdom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא against רבי אמי's objection. He took the money only to avoid trouble with the government.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא was not ignoring the פסוק. He had a strong practical reason: refusing a gift from the king's mother could anger the rulers and put the Jews in danger.

keyTerms.meaning: And רבא? (a short way of asking why רבא acted as he did)
Because of, for the sake of

phrases.english: And why did Rava accept?
For the sake of peace with the kingdom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אמי's objection by explaining רבא's motive.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא ignored the lesson of the פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא accepted the money only to keep peace with the government.

steps.title: Shouldn't רבי אמי also care about peace with the kingdom?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: רבי אמי should also have recognized the need for שלום מלכות, so why was he angry?
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי אמי too should agree that it was for peace with the kingdom!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: if רבא's reason was so good, why didn't רבי אמי accept it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Keeping peace with the government is an obvious concern that any חכם would agree to. So רבי אמי's anger needs explaining, since it seems he should have understood רבא.

phrases.english: But Rabbi Ami too should agree that it was
for the sake of peace with the kingdom!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אַמֵּי נָמֵי, מִשּׁוּם שְׁלוֹם מַלְכוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer for רבא into a question about רבי אמי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שלום מלכות is a reason everyone accepts, so רבי אמי should not have been upset.

steps.title: רבא should have given it to non-Jewish poor
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי's complaint was that רבא should have distributed the money to non-Jewish poor people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because רבא should have distributed it to the non-Jewish poor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what really bothered רבי אמי. Taking the money was fine, but it should have gone to non-Jewish poor people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now רבי אמי's position is narrower. He agrees with accepting the gift for peace. He only objects if Jewish poor people benefit, since that gives the nations merit through helping ישראל.

phrases.english: Because he should have distributed them
to the gentile poor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by narrowing what רבי אמי objected to.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אמי objected to accepting the money at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אמי agreed to accepting it, but held it must go to non-Jewish poor.

steps.title: רבא really did give it to non-Jewish poor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that רבא actually did give the money to non-Jewish poor, and begins to explain why רבי אמי was still angry.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא, too, gave it to the non-Jewish poor. And רבי אמי, who got angry, it was because...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reveals that רבא did exactly what רבי אמי wanted. It then starts to explain why רבי אמי was upset anyway; that explanation continues in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So there was no real disagreement between רבא and רבי אמי about what should be done. רבי אמי's anger must have come from something else, which the גמרא is about to say.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא accepted the queen mother's charity for שלום מלכות and gave it to non-Jewish poor. In practice, רבי אמי agreed this was the right thing to do.

phrases.english: And Rava, too,
gave them to the gentile poor;
and Rabbi Ami got angry because it was
phrases.notes: The sentence isn't finished here; the reason for his anger comes on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רבא already fulfilled רבי אמי's requirement, and sets up the true reason for the anger.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא gave the money to Jewish poor, against רבי אמי's view.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא gave it to non-Jewish poor; רבי אמי's anger has a different cause, explained next.
